title: Burst: improve deny error semantics (429 vs 503) + safe deny reason headers
author: Elena Popov
description:
Context: During burst beta/pilot, customers and Support reported confusion when burst was denied but the API returned 503 ("Service Unavailable"), which reads like an outage and triggers aggressive retries. See SUP-3277 and feedback from pilot check-ins. This PR clarifies semantics so clients can make correct retry decisions, and adds a safe, stable deny reason code for debugging without leaking internal topology/capacity details.

Behavior changes:
- When a request attempts Dedicated burst and is denied by policy/admission (limits, cooldown, circuit breaker, saturation gate), return HTTP 429 Too Many Requests (instead of 503).
  - Includes Retry-After (seconds) when we can compute it (cooldown/backoff); otherwise omitted.
  - Includes a *sanitized* reason code header: x-redwood-burst-deny-reason: <enum>.
  - Includes x-redwood-burst: denied (boolean-ish string) to make it easy to filter logs/client metrics.
- When we fail to evaluate admission due to internal errors (policy service unavailable/timeouts, router exceptions, unexpected deny reason), return HTTP 503 Service Unavailable.
  - Does NOT include raw error strings from internal services.

Header safety / redaction:
- New header allowlist for deny reasons. We only emit values from a fixed enum (no pool names, no region codes, no numeric thresholds).
- Removed previous behavior where we could forward a free-form deny message into headers in certain code paths.
- The deny reason is still available internally in structured logs/traces (burst.deny_reason_code) for forensics.

Deny reason enum (client-visible):
- not_enabled
- not_eligible
- tenant_limit
- cooldown
- pool_saturated
- circuit_breaker
- baseline_only (request routed to baseline because burst was not attempted)

Notes:
- This PR does not change routing/fallback selection logic; it only changes response mapping + headers when we end up returning an error to the caller.
- For requests that successfully fall back (e.g., baseline route succeeds or alternative region/model chosen), we do not return an error; we only annotate with x-redwood-burst: attempted/used when relevant.

Testing:
- Added integration tests for:
  - 429 mapping on deny-by-policy with/without Retry-After
  - 503 mapping on policy evaluation failure
  - header allowlist enforcement (unknown reasons are dropped)
  - regression: retries reusing context must not bypass status mapping
- Updated golden tests for error payload shape to ensure consistency across REST and streaming endpoints.

Rollout:
- Guarded by feature flag: burst_error_semantics_v2 (default OFF). SRE can enable per-tenant during pilot.
- After enabling, customer-visible change is primarily status code (503 -> 429) and headers; no change in request format.

Changed areas:
- services/router/burst/admission_result_to_http.go
- services/gateway/http/errors/burst_error_mapper.go
- services/router/headers/burst_headers.go
- services/router/tests/integration/burst_deny_semantics_test.go
- libs/observability/log_fields/burst.go

Commits:
- router: map burst denial to 429 + Retry-After
- gateway: standardize burst deny payload + header emission
- security: sanitize deny reasons (enum allowlist) and drop free-form header forwarding
- tests: add integration coverage + update golden fixtures
commits: router: map burst admission deny -> 429 and plumb Retry-After
gateway: normalize burst error payload fields and streaming path parity
headers: add deny reason allowlist + redact unsafe details
observability: emit burst.deny_reason_code in structured logs
tests: integration + golden updates for deny semantics
conversation:
Mina Haddad (review): Can we be explicit that 429 is "admission denied" vs "quota exceeded"? Also confirm we won't surface pool/region info in the reason.

Elena Popov (author): Yep. The reason header is from a fixed enum (no pool/region/thresholds). Payload message uses "Burst admission denied" wording and points clients to Retry-After if present.

Peter Holtz (review): Retry-After semantics: are we comfortable sending it only for cooldown? What about saturation/tenant_limit?

Elena Popov (author): Cooldown is the only case where we can provide a meaningful time-based retry hint today. For saturation/tenant_limit, we omit it to avoid implying a predictable recovery time.

Sean Gallagher (review): From an SRE perspective, 503 was paging us via client-side error budgets; 429 should reduce noise. Please ensure we still log enough detail for forensics.

Elena Popov (author): Added burst.deny_reason_code + burst.admission_result in router logs, and we keep the full internal reason in logs only (not headers).

Marcus Lin (security review): Please avoid forwarding any raw policy errors to headers; also ensure unknown deny reasons don't leak (e.g., default stringification).

Elena Popov (author): Addressed in latest push: explicit allowlist + drop-on-unknown. Added unit test that fails if a new reason is introduced without updating allowlist.

Logan Wright (review): For metrics parity, did we update the error label mapping to avoid exploding cardinality?

Elena Popov (author): Yes—metrics continue to use the same low-cardinality reason enum (same as header). No per-tenant labels added here.

Mina Haddad (final): LGTM with the allowlist + feature flag. Please call out in release notes when we flip it for pilot tenants.

Sean Gallagher (final): Approved; this will help with pilot support load.
